newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police say poison biscuit extortion over.
newsitem.headline: Australian police say poison biscuit extortion over.

text.p: Australian police said on Tuesday they were confident that a threat from an extortionist to poison biscuits in supermarkets along the country's east coast was over, but cautioned shoppers to remain vigilant.

"As far as our investigations are concerned, we are confident it (the threat) is over...but the public need to be cautious about the product they purchase," Queensland police superintendent Ron Pickering told a news conference.
Arnotts, Australia's biggest biscuit maker and the sole target of the extortionist's threat, announced its products would be back in stores from Wednesday.
"We are confident, based on the evidence, that it is now appropriate to return Arnott's biscuits to retail shelves," said Arnotts managing director Chris Roberts.
Arnotts withdrew all its products from shops in New South Wales and Queensland states on February 14, three days before the extortionist's deadline, and dumped millions of packets of biscuits.
"We estimate we have lost at least A$10 million (US$7.6 million) after deducting insurance proceeds and tax," said Roberts. "Our full loss will be known after further estimates are made."

Police had decided the extortion threat was over on the basis that the extortionist had not contacted them since issuing the threat on February 3. "Last Thursday, we decided to wait until Monday for any further contact from the extortionist. No contact was made," Pickering said.

The extortionist threatened to lace Arnotts biscuits with pesticide and plant them in stores in New South Wales and Queensland states from February 17 unless police involved in a 1991 murder case undertook a lie detector test.
The extortionist said police lied in giving evidence that resulted in Ron Thomas serving two life sentences for a double shooting murder Thomas says he did not commit.
A public appeal by Thomas for the extortionist to stop was also a factor in police declaring the extortion threat over, Pickering said.
However, police said they would continue their investigation into the extortion until they made an arrest.
"We are still treating this extortion as a major investigation," said New South Wales police superintendent Jock Milroy.
Arnotts is 70 percent owned by the Campbell Soup Co of the United States.
